note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Windows PowerShell 5.1 on CON-SRV02. The App Compatibility FOD needs Windows Update from CON-SRV01 (or the Languages and Optional Features ISO and Setup.FodSourcePath). The Nano Server part has no recording (shown as code in the video). Tear-down restores the pre-ep10 checkpoints.
prepare: foreach ($v in 'CON-SRV01', 'CON-SQL01', 'CON-CLI01') { if (-not (Get-VMSnapshot -VMName $v -Name pre-ep10 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Checkpoint-VM -Name $v -SnapshotName pre-ep10 } }
Invoke-Command -Session $s { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\lab | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\lab\ep10 -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

screens.name: sconfig
steps: Open the console of CON-SRV01 in VMConnect, signed in as the lab Administrator (typed off camera); SConfig is already on screen
Show the main menu with the server name and the domain in view
Type 4 (Configure remote management) and show the page behind it; do not change anything; go back
Type 15 for the PowerShell prompt; optionally show: Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like "ServerCore.AppCompatibility*"
Type exit to return to SConfig
mask: VMConnect title bar ("<VM> on <laptop name>") and the laptop taskbar

prepare: # CON-CLI01 is switched off for one screen: "off" and "WinRM broken" both read as no answer

screens.name: check-after
prepare: do { Start-Sleep -Seconds 10; $ok = try { Invoke-Command -VMName CON-SRV01 -Credential $cred { $true } -ErrorAction Stop } catch { $false } } until ($ok)
do { Start-Sleep -Seconds 10; $ok = try { Invoke-Command -VMName CON-CLI01 -Credential $cred { $true } -ErrorAction Stop } catch { $false } } until ($ok)
